stories.headline: Josh Allen scored 46.82 and the argument stopped being theoretical
stories.body:
Josh Allen was projected for 25.3 points on Thursday night and scored 46.82. Jared Goff was projected for 19.3 and scored 37.78. The two quarterbacks who played cleared their projections by a combined 40.0 points, which is not a rounding error and is not variance you shrug at.

The desk has spent two weeks saying the same thing: the public projections behind this page are built on a four-point passing touchdown, and this league pays six. Nobody had a result to point at. Now there are two, on the same night, from the only two quarterbacks who have played.

The beneficiaries are already on the board. Team Carlzyn sits on 46.72 almost entirely because of Allen — DJ Moore, projected 13.1, contributed minus 0.10. littlescot229 has 61.08 from Goff and Jahmyr Gibbs alone.

takes.text: Twenty-one and a half points over on Allen, eighteen and a half over on Goff. I have been saying three to four points a week per quarterback and I was conservative. Two data points is not proof. Two data points pointing the same direction on the same night, at the exact position I flagged, is not nothing either.

I said when the ruler is wrong you stop arguing about the inches. Thursday night was the ruler being wrong in public. Mason did not out-coach anybody. He rostered a quarterback in a league that pays six and the rest of you were reading a number built for a league that pays four.

Forty-six point eight two. From one man. On a Thursday. Mason Beebe is sitting on forty-six points and eight players still to go and I am supposed to believe this is a coin flip against Chase? Somebody call NABERS and tell him the coin landed.

DJ Moore was projected for 13.1 and scored negative zero point one. That is a thirteen-point swing in the wrong direction and Carlzyn still leads by forty-six. Some men are born lucky and some men start Josh Allen.
Everybody is looking at Allen. Look at DJ Moore. Negative zero point one. That is a man who has bottomed out, and there is only one direction available to him now. Buy low. Write it down.

stories.storyline: Does the six-point passing touchdown actually reshape quarterback value in this league, or does everyone keep drafting and starting as if it pays four?

stories.headline: Ian has 61.08 from two players and the week has barely started
stories.body:
littlescot229 started Jared Goff and Jahmyr Gibbs on Thursday and got 61.08 out of the pair — 37.78 and 23.30. Kool-Aid Man has not scored a point, because Kool-Aid Man has not had a player take the field.

The arithmetic from here is unkind. Ian has eight starters left projected for 85.1. Jace has all ten of his, projected for 125.4, and needs 146.1 from them to overhaul a lead built before Sunday.

Ian was sixth in the standings and mid-table in the power rankings. He is currently winning by sixty-one.

takes.text: I said littlescot229 was the team in this league nobody was looking at. Not fifth, not sixth. The team. And the desk treated me like I had wandered in off the street. He is up sixty-one points. I would like that noted somewhere permanent.

A 61.08 lead with eight starters left is worth less than it looks and considerably more than zero. The honest framing is that Jace now needs 146.1 from a roster projected for 125.4. Not impossible. Just not the plan anybody drew up.
Kool-Aid Man has scored ninety-eight points in one and a half weeks of football. At some stage we stop calling it a slow start and start calling it the ceiling.

stories.storyline: Is littlescot229 a genuine top-six team the desk underrated, or is a two-player Thursday about to be washed away on Sunday?

stories.headline: Cole left 22.50 on the bench before anybody else had kicked off
stories.body:
Dalton Kincaid scored 22.50 on The Dak Pack's bench on Thursday night. Cole is starting Travis Kelce at tight end, projected for 10.6 and yet to play. James Cook delivered 20.90 from the starting lineup, so the week is not a disaster — The Dak Pack leads Hunter I hardly know her! 20.90 to nothing.

It is the second week running. Cole finished Week 1 at 83% lineup efficiency, eleventh of twelve, with 26.4 points left unstarted. He is now two for two on leaving a tight end's worth of production on the bench.

Adam has his own small version of this, with Khalil Shakir posting 6.80 from the bench. It is a rounding error next to 22.50, but he trails by 20.90 and it would have covered a third of it.

takes.text: Twenty-two and a half points. On the bench. On a Thursday. Cole Hutchinson has now done this in consecutive weeks and I want somebody on that desk to explain to me how a man watches Kincaid go for twenty-two and still feels good about the tight end he submitted.

I have been in those locker rooms when a coach guesses wrong and the whole building knows before halftime. Nobody says anything. You just see it on the sideline. Cole is fine this week — Cook covered him. But twice is a habit forming, and habits are what beat you in November.

Eighty-three percent efficiency in Week 1 and 22.5 already outside the lineup in Week 2. I will not call it a pattern off two data points, but I will say that the points a manager leaves unstarted are the only ones he fully controls.

stories.storyline: Is Cole's lineup management a genuine structural problem, or two unlucky tight end calls that happen to have landed in a row?

stories.headline: Six matchups, six Thursday leaders, and the desk goes on the record
stories.body:
Every one of the six matchups is live and every one has a leader who got there before Sunday. Team Carlzyn leads I HURT MY NABERS 46.72 to nothing. F&F: Tokyo Swift leads Return of the King 35.20 to nothing, all of it from Amon-Ra St. Brown. The Dak Pack leads Hunter I hardly know her! 20.90 to nothing. Bakers Dozen leads davidbatista 17.20 to nothing on Sam LaPorta alone. Dsteady1234 leads Chop Wood, Carry Water 5.30 to nothing, which is the thinnest lead a man has ever had to defend.

The projections disagree with several of those leads. Chop Wood, Carry Water has all ten starters left at 133.3 against Darrien's nine at 118.7. davidbatista has ten left at 126.3 against Boesch's nine at 124.9. I HURT MY NABERS has ten left worth 132.6, and needs 144.4 of it.

So the desk is calling all six. On the record, before kickoff, scored on Monday like everything else here.

takes.text: Carlzyn, Tokyo Swift, Chop Wood, davidbatista, littlescot229 and The Dak Pack. The one that will look strange is David, who is behind and still has all ten of his men at 126.3 against Boesch's nine at 124.9. A seventeen-point head start off one tight end is not a lead. It is a man who happened to play on Thursday.

Carlzyn. Tokyo Swift. Chop Wood. Bakers Dozen. littlescot229. The Dak Pack. And I will say the thing nobody else will: Chase loses this week. He started the perfect lineup in Week 1 and it bought him a forty-six point hole against a man who started one quarterback.

Bakers Dozen, Chop Wood, Carlzyn, Tokyo Swift, The Dak Pack, littlescot229. That is the projection straight down with no editorialising: current score plus whatever each roster has left. It takes four Thursday leaders and two teams that are behind. Adam is the one people will argue about — he has 130.9 still to come against 114.5, but he is 20.90 down, and 16.4 of edge does not cover 20.9 of deficit. Close. Not a toss-up.

Carlzyn, Tokyo Swift, Chop Wood, Bakers Dozen, littlescot229, The Dak Pack. I am taking every single Thursday leader except one, because the lesson of this league so far is that the teams that are ahead stay ahead and the teams that are behind write long messages about variance.

littlescot229, Bakers Dozen, Dsteady1234, Return of the King, Hunter I hardly know her!, and I HURT MY NABERS. Four of those are trailing right now and that is exactly why. A deficit is stored energy. Write it down.

stories.storyline: Who has the best record when the desk's six called shots are scored on Monday?

stories.headline: The desk filed championship picks in week two, which is not when you file championship picks
stories.body:
Every analyst on this desk has now named one team to win the whole thing. They were asked on Friday of week two, because that is when the commissioner thought of it. Preseason predictions are traditionally made in the preseason.

Shannon Larp took F&F: Tokyo Swift, who put 199.76 on the board in week one. Stephen B Smith took Team Carlzyn, who managed 167.96 with obvious points still sitting on the bench. Mina Crimes took I HURT MY NABERS on the strength of a perfect week one lineup. Skip Baseless took Chop Wood, Carry Water, who nobody on this desk ranks higher than fourth and nobody ranks lower. Fat McCafferty took Bakers Dozen, who sit eleventh.

The picks are locked. Nobody gets to change one, nobody gets a second, and there is now a tab on this site that shows all five next to how that team is actually doing, for as long as the season lasts. Four of the five went to a team in the top four. The fifth is the reason this is worth having a tab for.

takes.text: Bakers Dozen. Eleventh today, and today is not the question I was asked. That roster has a schedule that opens up in November and a manager who drafts like he is owed something. Ask me in December. Write it down.

Chop Wood, Carry Water. Everybody in this building has them fourth and not one of them will say another word about it. Fourth is where you put a team when you want credit for noticing it without ever having to defend it. I am defending it. In December. Out loud.

I HURT MY NABERS, and the reasoning is unglamorous. A perfect lineup in week one is a process outcome, not a lucky one, and process is the only thing in this league that survives a bad month. Rosters get hurt. Habits do not.

CARLZYN. One hundred and sixty-seven point nine six in week one with points still on his bench, which means the ceiling on that roster is a number nobody in this league has seen yet. I am not being brave. I am reading.

Tokyo Swift. A hundred and ninety-nine in a week gets your attention, but that is not the reason. I have been on teams that had that feeling in week two, where nobody talks about the record because everybody in the building already knows. That is the one I want when it gets cold.

stories.storyline: Which of the five championship picks becomes genuinely embarrassing first?
